verses.1: And when Yabin the king of Hothar heard this, he sent messengers to Yoav, the king of Madon, and also to the kings of Shimer and Achshaf.
verses.2: And to the kings who are located on mountains and in deserts, where they live in darkness and misery.
verses.3: The Canaanites from the east and from the sea, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites – they live in the mountains, and the Hivvites live under the trees in the land of Egypt.
verses.4: And they went out, along with all their possessions. They were a large group of people, with many ships and carriages.
verses.5: And all these kings came together, and they arrived and stayed together at Me’irom, in order to fight against Israel.
verses.6: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them. For just as it is now, I will give them over into the hands of Israel. Their horses will be destroyed, and their chariots will be burned with fire.”
verses.7: And Joshua came, along with all the people who fought with him. They were attacked suddenly by enemy forces, and they fell to the ground.
verses.8: And Jehovah gave them into the hands of Israel. They pursued them until they reached their borders, as far as the waters and the edge of the sea. They continued to pursue them until they were completely destroyed.
verses.9: And Joshua did as Yahweh had commanded him: their horses and chariots were destroyed by fire.
verses.10: And in that time, Joshua sat down and gathered together the people. He struck Jericho with his spear. For Jericho was the first city of all these kings.
verses.11: And it destroyed all the souls that were inside it. According to the curse of the Lord, not a single soul was left alive. And its walls were burned by the fire.
verses.12: And all the cities of these kings, and all their rulers, Jehosua captured. He destroyed them according to the commandment given by Moses, the servant of Jehovah.
verses.13: Only those cities that stood on the banks of the river were destroyed by Israel. I destroyed their gates alone. Yehoshua destroyed them.
verses.14: And all the livestock in these cities and the animals there were killed by the children of Israel. But all people were killed by the sword until they were destroyed. No one was left alive.
verses.15: When Jehovah commanded Moses, Moses also commanded Joshua to do the same. And Joshua did not remove anything from what Jehovah had commanded Moses.
verses.16: And Joshua took all this land, including the mountains, all the hills, all the plains, and also the regions around Israel.
verses.17: From the mountain, the locusts began to fly down. They ate up all the kings and rulers under the tree of Horemon. They killed them all.
verses.18: For many days, Joshua fought against all these kings.
verses.19: There was no city that could fulfill the needs of the children of Israel. The inhabitants of Giv’on took everything away during the war.
verses.20: For from Jehovah’s command, it was decreed that their hearts should be strengthened for the battle against Israel, so that they would not become a refuge for them. This was in order to destroy them, as Jehovah commanded Moses.
verses.21: And in that time, Joshua came and destroyed those idols from the mountains, from their shrines, from all places where they worshipped them. He destroyed all the idols in Judah and Israel, along with their cities.
verses.22: No giants remained in the land of the Israelites. Only in Gaza, Gat, and Ashdod did some remain.
verses.23: And Joshua took all the land, just as God had told Moses. He gave it to Israel as their inheritance, in accordance with what God had commanded. The land was free from war.
